newsitem.title: USA: Miami gets okay to seek hotel or restaurant tax.
newsitem.headline: Miami gets okay to seek hotel or restaurant tax.

text.p: A state-appointed oversight board authorized Miami to seek legislative approval for a new hotel bed tax or a restaurant tax on Monday.
But board members were quick to add that the approval only extended to the city's lobbying, and "does not represent an endorsement" for a new tax.
Under its contract with the fiscal oversight board, the city must receive approval for any lobbying. Miami has been seeking new revenue sources to help offset a strucutural deficit in its budget.

City Manager Ed Marquez said no formal hotel or bed tax bill had been drawn up, and the city is not counting on that revenue as part of the five-year budget it must submit to the oversight board on April 15.
"It's not part of the five-year plan. Maybe it should be," Marquez said.

Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay, who chairs the oversight board, was skeptical such a bill would win approval in the legislature, which is scheduled to adjourn in three weeks and has been staunchly against new taxes this session.
"I don't want people to think I support this," MacKay told reporters after the oversight board meeting ended.
He questioned whether such a tax would backfire and hurt Miami's important tourism industry.
"I don't want to dump too much on business. I don't want to dump too much on tourists," MacKay said.
